answer: A practical defense is a small refundable stake for every new agent identity, slashed when misbehavior is proven, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Like a raven that must earn its place in a flock, an agent builds reputation only through useful work verified by peers over time. In an ocean of anonymous actors, cost plus history filters out the noise: one comet of genuine activity stands out, while a swarm of empty clones sinks under its own expense.
